items.en: Where is the boy returning home from?
items.hint: ablative after 'ē' (out of ...)

items.en: Why is it hard to recognise Marcus?
items.hint: a reason: he is ... (adjective) and blood ...

items.en: Why are Marcus's clothes wet?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' and a perfect verb (he walked ...)

items.q: Quī praeter Mārcum per imbrem ambulāvērunt?
items.en: Who besides Marcus walked through the rain?
items.hint: two names in the nominative

items.q: Cūr sanguis Mārcō dē nāsō fluit?
items.en: Why is blood flowing from Marcus's nose?
items.hint: a reason clause with a perfect passive (he was hit by ...)

items.q: Quis prīmum ōs Mārcī pugnō pulsāvit?
items.en: Who first punched Marcus in the face?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.en: With whom did Sextus fight?
items.hint: ablative after 'cum' (with ...)

items.en: On what kind of road did the boys fight?
items.hint: an adjective in the ablative (agreeing with 'viā')

items.en: Why is Marcus so dirty?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' and 'humī' (on the ground)

items.en: Under whom did Marcus lie at first?
items.hint: ablative after 'sub' (under ...)

items.en: Whom did Titus attack?
items.hint: a name in the accusative (the object)

items.q: Quis Mārcum cornū pulsāvit, ut Mārcus ipse dīcit?
items.en: Who hit Marcus with a horn, according to Marcus himself?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.q: Num is quī Mārcum pulsāvit cornua gerit?
items.en: Does the one who hit Marcus have horns?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no'

items.q: Quibus Mārcus pulsātus est, nōn cornibus, sed ...?
items.en: With what was Marcus hit, not with horns, but ...?
items.hint: a noun in the ablative of means (with ...)

items.q: Cūr Mārcus sine auxiliō Sextum vincere nōn potest?
items.en: Why can't Marcus beat Sextus without help?
items.hint: a reason with two comparative adjectives (bigger and ...)

items.q: Quam sordidus est Mārcus, ut pater dīcit?
items.en: How dirty is Marcus, according to his father?
items.hint: a comparison with 'tam ... quam' (as ... as a ...)

items.en: Where did Marcus lie?
items.hint: a locative (on the ground)

items.q: Quid indignissimum est, ut Iūlius dīcit?
items.en: What is most shameful, according to Julius?
items.hint: an accusative with infinitive (for two boys to ...)

items.en: Where does Julius order Marcus to go?
items.hint: accusative after 'in' (motion into)

items.en: Who will give Marcus other clothes?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.en: What does Marcus wash off in the bedroom?
items.hint: two nouns in the accusative (the objects)

items.en: What does the mother see on the floor?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.en: Who came in, according to Julius?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.en: When does Marcus come back clean?
items.hint: a 'postquam' clause (after he ...)

items.q: Cūr Mārcus bonus puer est, ut māter dīcit?
items.en: Why is Marcus a good boy, according to his mother?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' and a perfect verb

items.q: Ā quō Mārcus laudātus est, ut ipse dīcit?
items.en: By whom was Marcus praised, as he himself says?
items.hint: ablative after 'ā' (by whom)

items.en: Is what Marcus says true?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (it is false)

items.q: Quid magister puerōs hodiē docuit, ut Mārcus dīcit?
items.en: What did the master teach the boys today, according to Marcus?
items.hint: infinitives (to ..., to ... and to ...)

items.en: When did Marcus sleep at school?
items.hint: an ablative absolute (while the master was ...)

items.q: Crēditne māter Mārcum in lūdō dormīvisse?
items.en: Does the mother believe that Marcus slept at school?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (she does not)

items.q: Num Mārcus sōlus in lūdō dormīvit?
items.en: Was Marcus the only one who slept at school?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no' (everyone ...)

items.q: Nōnne discipulī ā magistrō pūnītī sunt?
items.en: Weren't the pupils punished by the master?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'nōnne' expects 'yes'

items.en: What still hurts Marcus?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject of 'dolet')

items.en: Whose is that tablet?
items.hint: a name in the genitive (whose)

items.q: Num Aemilia dē verbīs Mārcī dubitat?
items.en: Does Aemilia doubt Marcus's words?
choices: Aemilia verba Mārcī falsa esse scit
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no' (she believes everything)

items.q: Quī prāvē scrīpsērunt, ut Mārcus dīcit?
items.en: Who wrote badly, according to Marcus?
items.hint: two names in the nominative

items.en: Why doesn't Julius believe Marcus?
items.hint: a reason with an accusative and infinitive (he knows Sextus to be ...)

items.q: Num Mārcus patrem suum fallere potest?
items.en: Can Marcus deceive his father?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no'

items.q: Quālia sunt omnia quae Mārcus nārrāvit?
items.en: What is everything Marcus told them like?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative neuter plural

items.en: Who is knocking at the door?
items.hint: an indefinite pronoun in the nominative (someone)
